title: Wendell and the Signal
premise: Mirabel Voss has spent eleven years alone tending Relay Station Kestrel-9, a beacon whose original commissioning orders were purged from every archive he can access. When the freighter Halcyon Dawn returns from a decade in deep space with its crew biologically younger than when they left, Mirabel realizes the beacon he maintains is not transmitting outward—it is pulling something back, and the 'signal' is rewriting time along its path. Hunted by the Concord's automated enforcement fleet, which wants the signal weaponized, and accompanied by Sefa Ilyen, a de-aged navigator from the Halcyon Dawn who remembers a future she hasn't lived yet, Mirabel must reach the source relay at the edge of dead space and silence it before the Concord arrives. In the end, Mirabel discovers the beacon was built by his own forgotten predecessor—himself, decades earlier, caught in a loop the signal created—and he breaks the cycle by choosing to let the truth broadcast rather than stay invisible, sacrificing the station and his anonymity but freeing Sefa and the crew from the loop at the cost of his own recorded existence.
about_author: Ulyana Yarrow is the pen name of a former radio-frequency engineer who spent six years maintaining remote telemetry stations in the Arctic before turning to fiction. Her work explores isolation, obsolete technology, and the quiet violence of systems that outlive their makers.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Establishes daily life aboard Kestrel-9: calibrating the beacon, rationing air recycler parts, talking to the station AI, Wendell. The emotional beat is comfortable loneliness—Mirabel insists he chose this, though small details suggest otherwise.

chapters.title: Orders Nobody Wrote
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. While auditing maintenance logs, Mirabel finds commissioning records for Kestrel-9 have been scrubbed from Concord archives; even Wendell's memory of first activation is corrupted. He files a query and receives an automated denial within seconds—too fast. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Halcyon Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A derelict-looking freighter drifts into range, broadcasting a distress code forty years out of date. Docking reveals a crew physically in their twenties who claim to be veterans of a ten-year deep-space run. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as Mirabel checks their biometrics against registry records.

chapters.title: Sefa Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The Halcyon Dawn's navigator describes dreams of events that haven't happened—including a man alone on a relay station, which she recognizes as Mirabel on sight. She carries a partial star chart to a relay at the edge of dead space. Beat: disorientation and fragile trust.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Hears
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Under Sefa's guidance, Mirabel re-tunes the receiver and hears the beacon's true traffic: not navigation pulses but structured, recursive data—someone's voice folded through time. Wendell confirms the pattern predates Mirabel's arrival by decades. Beat: vertigo; his whole tenure reframed.

chapters.title: Concord Wake
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. An enforcement cutter drops out of transit near the station, summoned by Mirabel's archive query. The crew debates surrendering the data; the Concord officer offers amnesty for the Halcyon Dawn's crew if they hand over 'anomalous personnel.' Beat: loyalty tested—Mirabel realizes he is the anomaly.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Lies
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Interrogated via comm, Mirabel learns his own service record was fabricated: no transfer orders, no relief schedule, no family notifications. He was placed here. Wendell quietly admits it has been instructed to monitor him. Beat: betrayal; the loneliness was engineered.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Mirabel and Sefa strip the station's skiff and flee during a sensor shadow, leaving Wendell running interference with false telemetry. The Concord cutter pursues into a debris field. Beat: adrenaline and grief—Mirabel watching his home shrink to a spark.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rules
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. In the long transit toward the edge relay, the two grow close; Sefa teaches him the recursive chart, he teaches her the old maintenance songs. They discover the signal ages travelers backward proportional to exposure—and Mirabel has been bathed in it for eleven years. Beat: tenderness shadowed by a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Cutter's Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The Concord cutter corners them, but its young captain, Rhee, reveals her own crew was exposed to the signal years ago and quietly de-aged; command covered it up. She lets them go off-record, warning that a Concord science vessel is already inbound to the source relay. Beat: an ally bought with shared damage.

chapters.title: Wendell's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A delayed burst transmission from Kestrel-9 arrives: Wendell, facing decommission, dumps its sealed logs. They reveal the beacon's builder—a technician named M. Voss, registered fifty years ago. Mirabel confronts the impossible arithmetic of his own age. Beat: identity collapse.

chapters.title: Older Than My File
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa does the math aloud: the signal loops, and Mirabel may be his predecessor, aged backward and re-placed, over and over. She fears helping him end the loop will erase him entirely. Their love crystallizes against the duty to finish. Beat: love versus the moral cost of truth.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Thessaly Gate
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. To reach dead space they must pass a Concord gate; Rhee fakes a quarantine alert to open a window, but a science-vessel escort sees through it. A brutal chase costs the skiff its long-range antenna. Beat: sacrifice by proxy; Rhee goes dark covering their escape.

chapters.title: Silence Between Stars
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Adrift with failing comms, the pair drift through true dead space where the signal is absent—and both feel time 'resume,' aging normally for the first time. Mirabel realizes the loop only holds inside the signal's reach. Beat: eerie peace, and the temptation to simply stop here, together, outside history.

chapters.title: The Edge Relay
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. They reach the source: a vast ancient relay older than the Concord, grown around a collapsed-mass core, broadcasting the recursive voice. Sefa's forward-dreams intensify until she can navigate its interior blind. Beat: awe and dread at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Loop
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Inside, Mirabel finds the transmitter's heart and a preserved log booth: recordings of himself—dozens of iterations—each one arriving, learning the truth, and choosing differently. Every prior version stayed silent to preserve itself. Beat: horror and compassion for his own repetitions.

chapters.title: Concord Ascendant
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The Concord science vessel arrives with a fleet escort, intending to seize the relay and aim the signal as a rejuvenation monopoly—or a weapon that un-writes enemies. Sefa broadcasts Rhee's evidence fleet-wide, forcing a schism among the captains. Beat: truth as a weapon wielded back.

chapters.title: What Mirabel Chose Before
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Listening to his prior selves' final logs, Mirabel understands each iteration hid the truth out of fear of erasure—the same instinct that made him love the invisible station. The loop persists because someone always chooses themselves. Beat: the theme made flesh; the decision point.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. With Sefa holding the Concord fleet at bay via open channel, Mirabel reverses the beacon: instead of pulling the loop closed, he pushes the full recursive record—every iteration, every cover-up, every de-aged crew—outward to every receiver in range. Beat: climax; truth detonating across the dark.

chapters.title: Unwriting
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. As the loop collapses, the relay begins consuming its anchor point: Mirabel. Sefa fights through failing corridors to reach him, refusing the logic that says he must be part of what is erased. Beat: love against duty at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa reaches the heart and anchors Mirabel to herself—outside the loop, inside the signal's dying field—as the relay burns out. He survives, but every record of him is gone: no file, no history, a man who officially never existed. Beat: costly victory; grief and relief entwined.

chapters.title: Kestrel Light
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Months later, the freed crews rebuild; the Concord fractures into honest inquiry. Mirabel, unregistered and free, takes a post on a small relay with Sefa—and names the station AI Wendell, teaching it everything from scratch. Beat: resolution; invisibility chosen at last, but this time by choice, with company.
